terms.meaning: A system that gives judgements based on laws.
Rules that regulate behaviour, control crime, keep order and protect citizens' rights.
A people's court that settles cases by compromise, quickly and cheaply.
A complaint by an affected citizen against a government body that breaks the law; the court takes it up without fees.

items.name: Functions of the courts
items.formula: Interpret laws and settle disputes between people, and between people and government.
items.example: They are independent of the legislature and executive.

items.name: Levels of courts in India
items.formula: Supreme Court (national, New Delhi), High Courts (state), Subordinate Courts (district, magistrate, Lok Adalats).
items.example: Appeals go from lower to higher courts.

items.name: Supreme Court make-up
items.formula: The Chief Justice of India and 33 other judges, all appointed by the President.
items.example: 1 + 33 = 34 judges in all; it sits in New Delhi.

items.name: Who can be a Supreme Court judge
items.formula: A High Court judge for at least five years, a High Court advocate for ten years, or a distinguished jurist.

items.name: Functions of the Supreme Court
items.formula: Settles Centre-State and inter-State disputes, issues writs for fundamental rights, interprets the Constitution.
items.example: It advises the President when asked.

items.name: High Courts
items.formula: The highest court of a state; India has 25; Karnataka's is in Bengaluru.
items.example: Judges retire at 62; English or a regional language may be used.

items.name: Who can be a High Court judge
items.formula: A citizen with ten years in the judiciary or ten years as a High Court advocate.
items.example: The President appoints the Chief Justice after consulting the Chief Justice of India and the Governor.

items.name: Civil and criminal courts
items.formula: Civil: money, property and contracts. Criminal: murder, theft and robbery.
items.example: Both are subordinate courts under the High Court.

items.name: How a Lok Adalat works
items.formula: Only parties who agree to settle; its judgement is final and binding, with no appeal.
items.example: Anyone forced into a compromise can complain to the police.

items.name: Protection for the President
items.formula: Can't be arrested or face a criminal case during the term.
items.example: Decisions made in office can't be questioned in court.

mistakes.text: Supreme Court judges retire at 65; High Court judges at 62.
There is no appeal against a Lok Adalat judgement, unlike other courts.
A property dispute goes to a civil court; a theft goes to a criminal court.
